references.role: Recognizable white/orange underwater train body, dark continuous window band, jointed two sections; convert into rear-facing nose and opening outer arm shell.
Complete core's huge orange mechanical fist and gray articulated fingers, body-independent arm identity.
Required massive fist/forearm weight only; do not copy the full body or forward bomber nose as arm nose.

prompt: Use case: stylized-concept / mechanical production design. Create a clean, precisely readable three-panel mechanical concept sheet for ONE transformable underwater-train forearm weapon, not the whole robot. Landscape sheet, three equally sized panels in a single row on pale warm paper; NO written text, labels, logos or numbers. Style: KINETIC_CEL, crisp pressure-varied ink outlines, large clean orange / ivory / steel-gray planes, two hard cel-shading steps, no gritty photoreal surface or busy background. Input1 is the submarine train design source; input2 is the core robot's massive fist identity; input3 gives the strengthened fist/forearm mass. The structure must follow a single consistent object across all three views. All panels have the SAME direction: REAR is LEFT, attack/hand/barrel opening is RIGHT. Panel1: side three-quarter view of one separated white/orange train section, low streamlined cab nose points LEFT; its separated middle end is on the RIGHT. Preserve black cab glass, orange stripe and side window band. Panel2: the same section's LONG middle shell opens into two hinged lateral half-shells, one on each side; the closed pointed cab at the LEFT stays recognizably a train nose, not a gun muzzle. A hefty gray robot forearm and enormous orange cuff with gray clenched fist are shown immediately beneath as the inner carried structure, and its knuckles point RIGHT. The hinge and saddle relationship is simple and visible. Panel3: finished forearm assembly shown with the forearm raised horizontally, elbow on LEFT, enormous clenched fist on RIGHT. The strengthened orange forearm and actual fist MUST be visible as a complete inner arm. The opened white train half-shells mount OUTSIDE that strengthened forearm, one on each side, creating a split tubular cannon housing; their circular dark emitter lips face RIGHT along the arm. The pointed train CAB end sits back near/beyond the ELBOW and points LEFT, away from the knuckles. The fist projects a little beyond the front housing and remains the main striking feature. Never turn the cab windshield into the forward muzzle, never point a train nose forward with the fist, never replace the fist by a barrel, never put the weapon at the pelvis or leg. Do not add engines, wings, extra fists, drills, cables or unrelated components. Keep identical shell colors/windows/number of major panels across the closed, opening and mounted states. Use generous space around each object; no exploded debris, action sparks, energy glows or arrows obscuring the joint.
